correctness.rationale: The coefficient hyperplane splits into the two independent within-block contrast spaces and the block-normal line. Covariance with replacement of k-subsets gives exact two frame eigenvalues; exact arithmetic independently reproduces 30 shell matrices. The ratio is strictly increasing in the parity-restricted integer shell offset squared. Integer inequalities yield the sharp \(1+1/(2k+1)\) floor and the complete odd-square equality family. A uniformly valid expansion at the unique real crossing, and explicit odd-integer subsequences, prove the stated liminf and limsup. Noninjective boundary cases are excluded from the optimum and treated separately. Finite checks do not certify an infinite theorem.

value.rationale: Distance shells are a natural, highly constrained graph-sampling geometry, and stable recovery of all first harmonics requires controlling the squared frame condition number. The theorem optimizes this quantity over every admissible shell for each balanced Johnson graph, establishes a sharp global stability obstruction and exact equality family, and resolves two distinctly scaled asymptotic extremal subsequences. This is a structural design result rather than a fixed-parameter covariance exercise; it gives precise quantitative selection guidance without claiming a downstream application theorem.
